prompt.en: Explain why archaeology is essential for reconstructing the human past. Give three reasons.

label.en: Material remains are the only source for more than 99 per cent of the human past

level1.en: Compare how long humans have made tools with how long humans have written anything down.

clue.en: Toolmaking goes back about 3 million years; writing appears only about 5,000 years ago, so almost the whole span leaves no documents at all.

level2Template.en: For more than ___ of the human past there are no written records at all, so material remains are the only source available for that period.

label.en: Excavated objects reveal how people actually lived, even with no written record

level1.en: Think about what a trench recovers: bones, seeds, tools, hearths, wall footings. What does each of those tell you?

clue.en: Diet, technology, trade contacts, the layout of a settlement and even the health of a body can all be read off excavated material.

level2Template.en: Tools, bones, seeds and building remains recovered by excavation reveal how people ___, even where nothing was ever written down.

accepted: obtained food, made tools and built their homes

label.en: A script can survive and still be unread, leaving objects as the main evidence

level1.en: The Harappans did write. Does that mean we can read what they wrote?

clue.en: The Sindhu lipi survives on thousands of seals and remains undeciphered, so their material remains still carry the whole account of their lives.

level2Template.en: Even where a script survives, it may remain ___, as the Sindhu lipi does, so objects stay the main evidence for those lives.

text.en: Archaeology is the study of the human past through material remains, and it is indispensable for three connected reasons.
For more than ___ of the human past there are no written records at all, so material remains are the only source available for that period.
Tools, bones, seeds and building remains recovered by excavation reveal how people ___, even where nothing was ever written down.
Even where a script survives, it may remain ___, as the Sindhu lipi does, so objects stay the main evidence for those lives.
